reviewed_arguments: Inverse gluing uses a neighborhood of the closed cutoff support; induction retains matrix order and all mixed derivatives.
Enhanced tangential derivatives are an explicit additional symbol assumption, not inferred from the ordinary mixed bound.
The phase-dual metric has the factor4/t^2; G12-G13 constants are uniform for |t|<=2, and the zero parameter is handled directly.
Compact approximants have uniform mixed seminorms; actual distributional multipliers and complete-seminorm Taylor bounds prove parameter differentiation.
The bilinear Gauss transform treats external parameters explicitly; diagonal derivatives add the exact normal and tangential losses.
The ordered integral remainder proves distinct tangential and full-frequency improvements; the exact Fourier-shift counterexample rules out their conflation.
Actual Schwartz products and adjoints pass through bounded approximants, giving one common distributional operator.
Mixed weight conjugation yields bounded derivatives; the earlier packet proof supplies L2 boundedness without an unsupported isotropic symbol-class assumption.
All real Sobolev domains use proved onto multipliers and Schwartz density; extensions agree as tempered distributions.
The exact metric ellipses preserve scales and are explicitly distinguished from characteristic sets.
